s:
Consider the following statements about human rights:
1. Human rights are inherent and inalienable to every human being.
2. In India every human right is also a Fundamental Right.
3. The Vienna Declaration (1993) affirmed that human rights are indivisible and interdependent.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: every Fundamental Right is a human right, but not every human right is a Fundamental Right.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): In India the right to vote is not a Fundamental Right.
Reason (R): The right to vote in India is a statutory right under Section 62 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true and R explains A: the right to vote, a political right, is only a statutory right (Sec. 62, RP Act 1951), not part of Part III.

s:
Match List-I (Document / event) with List-II (Year):
List-I | List-II
a. Magna Carta | i. 1688
b. Glorious Revolution, England | ii. 1215
c. US Declaration of Independence | iii. 1776
d. French Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen | iv. 1789
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Magna Carta – 1215 (King John); Glorious Revolution – 1688 (Bill of Rights 1689); US Declaration of Independence – 1776; French Declaration of the Rights of Man – 1789.

s:
Consider the following statements about the UDHR:
1. It was adopted by the UN General Assembly on 10 December 1948 in Paris.
2. The committee that drafted it was chaired by Eleanor Roosevelt.
3. Human Rights Day on 10 December was fixed by UNGA resolution 423(V) in 1948.
4. It consists of a Preamble and 30 articles.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: resolution 423(V) fixing Human Rights Day was passed in 1950, not 1948.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): The UDHR is legally binding on all UN member States.
Reason (R): The UDHR is a declaration adopted by a UN General Assembly resolution, not a treaty.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: A is false: as a declaration the UDHR is not legally binding. R is true: it was adopted as a UNGA resolution (10 Dec 1948) and is not a treaty.

s:
Match List-I (UDHR Article) with List-II (Right):
List-I | List-II
a. Article 3 | i. Work
b. Article 12 | ii. Life, liberty and security
c. Article 23 | iii. Education
d. Article 26 | iv. Privacy
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Art. 3 – life, liberty, security; Art. 12 – privacy (also ICCPR Art. 17); Art. 23 – work; Art. 26 – education.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The theme of Human Rights Day 2016 was 'Our Rights, Our Future, Right Now'.
2. The theme of Human Rights Day 2025 was 'Human Rights, Our Everyday Essentials'.
3. Universal Children's Day on 20 November marks the adoption of the UNCRC in 1989.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: 'Our Rights, Our Future, Right Now' was the 2024 theme; the 2016 theme was 'Stand up for someone's rights today'.

s:
Consider the following statements about the generations of human rights:
1. Karel Vasak proposed the three-generation classification in 1977.
2. Third-generation rights are linked with the ideal of fraternity.
3. Eradication of social discrimination is a first-generation right.
4. Social security is a second-generation right.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1, 2 and 4 are correct. 3 is wrong: eradication of social discrimination is a second-generation (equality) right; first-generation rights are civil and political.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The International Bill of Human Rights comprises the UDHR, the ICCPR, the ICESCR and the optional protocols.
2. The ICCPR entered into force before the ICESCR.
3. India acceded to both Covenants in 1979 but has not signed the ICCPR First Optional Protocol.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the ICESCR entered into force first (3 Jan 1976), the ICCPR on 23 Mar 1976.

s:
Match List-I (ICCPR Article) with List-II (Right):
List-I | List-II
a. Article 6 | i. Fair trial
b. Article 7 | ii. Life
c. Article 14 | iii. Freedom from torture
d. Article 19 | iv. Expression
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: ICCPR: Art. 6 – life; Art. 7 – no torture; Art. 14 – fair trial; Art. 19 – expression (privacy is Art. 17, child rights Art. 24).

s:
Match List-I (Convention) with List-II (Subject):
List-I | List-II
a. CERD | i. Persons with disabilities
b. CMW | ii. Enforced disappearance
c. CPED | iii. Migrant workers
d. CRPD | iv. Racial discrimination
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: CERD (1965) – racial discrimination, ratified by India 1968; CMW (1990) – migrant workers, not signed; CPED (2006) – enforced disappearance, signed 2007; CRPD (2006) – disabilities, ratified 2007.

s:
Consider the following statements about India and UN human rights treaties:
1. CEDAW was adopted in 1979 and ratified by India in 1993.
2. India ratified the Convention against Torture in 1997.
3. India acceded to the CRC on 11 December 1992.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: India signed the CAT in 1997 but has not ratified it.

s:
Consider the following statements about the UN Human Rights Council:
1. It was set up in 2006 in place of the UN Commission on Human Rights and is based in Geneva.
2. Its 47 members are elected by the UNGA for four-year terms.
3. A member can serve at most two consecutive terms.
4. A member can be suspended by a two-thirds vote of the UNGA.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: HRC members serve three-year terms.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Universal Periodic Review, a peer review of every UN member's record, began in 2008 in cycles of about 4.5 years.
2. Special rapporteurs under the special procedures are paid UN staff.
3. The OHCHR was set up in 1993 after the Vienna Conference.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: special rapporteurs are unpaid independent experts.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Paris Principles were drafted in Paris in October 1991 and adopted by the UNGA in 1993.
2. The Paris Principles require an NHRI to depend on the executive for investigations.
3. GANHRI accredits NHRIs through its Sub-Committee on Accreditation; 'A' status means fully compliant.
4. India's NHRC is a constitutional NHRI.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the Principles require independence, autonomy and powers to investigate. 4 is wrong: the NHRC (1993) is a statutory body under the PHRA 1993.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): The right to a clean, healthy and sustainable environment is a third-generation (collective) human right.
Reason (R): The UN General Assembly recognised the Right to Water and Sanitation on 28 July 2010.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true – a healthy environment is a collective, third-generation right (UNGA recognition 28 July 2022), and water and sanitation was recognised on 28 July 2010 – but R does not explain A.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Amnesty International was founded in London in 1961 by Peter Benenson.
2. Amnesty International received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1987.
3. Human Rights Watch is a New York-based NGO.
4. The UN Human Rights Prize is given by the UNGA, usually every five years, since 1968.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1, 3 and 4 are correct. 2 is wrong: Amnesty received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1977.
